title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of week lost. Historical closure weeks show ~14% demand drop in similar products.

drivers.name: Price increase (+4.1%)
drivers.evidence: Past price hikes (avg +3.5%) show median demand drop of -10% (noise-adjusted estimate).

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 25.3. The store closes Monday, reducing the selling period by 1/7. The price increased by 4.1%, which historically correlates with a demand drop. Recent weeks show no promotion or seasonal ramp, and the baseline already reflects the post-Labor Day decline. The price hike is a named driver with negative effect; past price increases show demand suppression. The closure is a clear demand reducer. No promotion or event uplift is expected. The classical model's 1.00 is unadjusted for these known drivers. Evidence is consistent but limited to one past closure and a few price changes.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 25.3 | 5%-95%: 4.7 - 53.3 | 10%-90%: 8.9 - 39.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
